newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ says copper market is tight.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ says copper market is tight.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd said on Thursday that the global copper market remained physically tight and that the mid-1996 slide in prices was an over-reaction to the Sumitomo trading scandal.
"The way the copper price fell in June was an over-reaction," executive chairman Robert Wilson told a news conference after the Anglo-Australian miner released its calendar 1996 results.
Wilson described the copper market as "still tight physically".
He said he would not speculate on the copper price.

The company is the minority partner in the giant Escondida mine in Chile which is operated by Australia's Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd. BHP has 57.5 percent of the mine, the world's largest copper producer, while the RTZ-CRA group has 30 percent.
RTZ-CRA said in a statement accompanying its results that group annual copper production rose 19 percent to 759,200 tonnes in 1996 but the average price fell 22 percent to 104 U.S. cents a pound.
"Market confidence was shaken by Sumitomo's announcement in June of losses due to unauthorised trading," it said.
